bib.title: Anemoi: A Semi-Centralized Multi-agent System Based on Agent-to-Agent Communication MCP server from Coral Protocol

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Anemoi: A Semi-Centralized Multi-agent System Based on Agent-to-Agent Communication MCP server from Coral Protocol", Xinxing Ren, Caelum Forder, Qianbo Zang et al. (Coral Protocol, Brunel, SnT Luxembourg, Hull), arXiv:2508.17068v3 [cs.MA], 10 Oct 2025. Marked "Preprint" (not peer reviewed). Authors are from the vendor, Coral Protocol, which also funded the work.
COVERAGE: 41171 of 41171 chars read, all 15 pages including Appendix A and B (case-study transcripts). Nothing skipped. The appendix B transcript ends mid-dialogue in the extraction (a "give up" answer is shown).

CLAIMS
1. Anemoi, with a small GPT-4.1-mini planner, scores higher on GAIA validation than the reproduced OWL under identical models and tools.
 number: 52.73% vs 43.64% (abstract says 43.63%), +9.09 points
 setup: GAIA validation set (165 tasks implied by the percentages, not stated), pass@3. Planner is GPT-4.1-mini, workers are GPT-4o, same OWL worker toolkits and prompts. OWL was reproduced on CAMEL 0.2.70, and Whisper is excluded from both.
 quote: "Anemoi achieved 52.73% accuracy with a small LLM (GPT-4.1-mini) as the planner, surpassing the strongest open-source baseline OWL (43.63%) by +9.09% under identical LLM settings."
 where: abstract (p1); Table 3 (p7)
2. Anemoi also beats the originally reported OWL (GPT-4o-mini planner) and several systems that use stronger LLMs.
 number: 47.27% for OWL as reported; +5.46 points
 setup: same GAIA validation, pass@3. Table 3 per-level scores: Anemoi L1 71.70, L2 52.33, L3 15.38. OWL-rep L1 61.54, L2 42.53, L3 11.54. OWL (original) L3 is 19.23, and Anemoi's L3 is lower than OWL's and than several other systems. Other baselines: Magnetic-One (o1) 46.06, HuggingFace Agents (GPT-4o) 44.24, Barcelona v0.1 (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) 50.30 (best proprietary).
 quote: "outperforming OWL with GPT-4o-mini and our reproduced OWL with GPT-4.1-mini by +5.46 and +9.09 percentage points, respectively."
 where: p7, Section 4.3
3. Task-level comparison with OWL: the gains are mostly attributed to collaborative refinement, but the authors' own breakdown shows that stochastic worker behaviour explains a large share.
 number: 25 tasks solved only by Anemoi, 10 solved only by OWL. Of the 25: 52% collaborative refinement, 8% reduced context redundancy, 40% stochastic worker behaviour. Of the 10: 90% stochastic worker behaviour, 10% web-agent latency.
 setup: same as claim 1. The attribution looks like a manual or authors' judgement (the method is not described).
 quote: "Anemoi successfully solved 25 tasks that OWL failed to answer, while OWL solved 10 tasks that Anemoi did not."
 where: p7-8, Sec 5.1, Fig 3
4. Remaining 68 Anemoi errors by cause.
 number: LLM capability 45.6%, toolkit limits 20.6%, incorrect plans 11.8%, communication latency 10.3%, annotation mistakes 7.4%, hallucination 4.4%
 setup: GAIA validation, Anemoi with GPT-4.1-mini planner.
 quote: "Errors caused by communication latency account for 10.3%; these are primarily due to the web agent occasionally taking excessive time to complete search tasks, during which it cannot respond to other agents' queries."
 where: p8-9, Sec 5.2, Fig 4
5. Design (qualitative): semi-centralized means the planner only writes the initial plan, and then all agents talk over a thread-based A2A MCP server. The authors claim three benefits: less planner dependence, continuous plan updates, and multi-agent debate. These are asserted. No ablation isolates each one, and token or cost savings are claimed but never measured.
 quote: "the planner provide initial plan, while workers coordinate directly to monitor progress, resolve bottlenecks, and propose refinements, and all agents are allowed to communicate directly"
 where: p2, Sec 1
 Protocol workflow (Sec 3.3): (1) agent discovery, (2) planner creates a thread and broadcasts plan π0 with allocation, (3) workers execute while a critique agent labels results accept or uncertain, (4) consensus vote approve/reject by all participants on candidate R*, (5) the answer-finding agent submits.
 Agents: Planner, Critique, Answer-Finding, plus three OWL-derived workers (Web, Document Processing, Reasoning & Coding).
 MCP primitives: list_agents, create_thread, add_participant / remove_participant, send_message, wait_for_mentions, close_thread. "contextual compartmentalization" via threads.
6. Baseline characterisation (qualitative): centralized baselines (Agent KB, Cognitive Kernel-Pro, OWL) use "context engineering" with unidirectional prompt passing and a predefined planner. The paper's Table 1 labels them Centralized and Anemoi Semi-centralized. Claim: planner dependence makes small planners degrade (cited to GAIA, [10]). The paper does not itself measure OWL with different planner sizes beyond the reproduced GPT-4.1-mini and the reported GPT-4o-mini.
 where: p1-3

LIMITS
- Single benchmark (GAIA validation), single planner model (GPT-4.1-mini), single worker model (GPT-4o). No strong-planner experiment, so "reduces dependence on the planner" is not tested directly. Anemoi is never run with a strong planner, and no planner-size sweep is given.
- No ablations: nothing separates the A2A channel, critique agent, consensus vote or plan updating. The added Critique and Answer-Finding agents mean extra roles and compute versus OWL. No token, cost or latency numbers are reported, even though token overhead is argued as a benefit.
- pass@3 is used, with no variance or repeated seeds. The authors concede 40% of the wins come from stochastic worker behaviour, and 90% of OWL-only wins are stochastic. That is close to noise-level evidence for the topology effect. Level 3 is worse than OWL's original.
- OWL was reproduced by the authors on a newer CAMEL version. They concede it scores lower than the original GPT-4o-mini OWL because Whisper was removed.
- GPT-4o-mini planner was not tried because it "lacked sufficient capability to reliably understand and correctly use the toolkits provided by the A2A MCP server". This shows the decentralised protocol has its own minimum capability floor.
- Failure mode: a busy worker cannot respond, so the others bypass it (latency, 10.3% of errors). Appendix B shows a deadlock-like loop where the planner, answer-finder and critic repeatedly ping an unresponsive web agent and finally answer "give up".
- Vendor paper promoting its own protocol. Proprietary scores come from the leaderboard and are not matched in setup.
- "Semi-centralized" is not formally defined; the planner still creates the thread and the initial plan.

BUILDS ON
- OWL (Hu et al., arXiv 2505.23885, 2025): the baseline, with worker agents and toolkits reused.
- Coral Protocol (Georgio et al., arXiv 2505.00749, 2025): A2A MCP server.
- MCP (Anthropic, Nov 2024).
- GAIA (Mialon et al., ICLR 2024; printed as 2023).
- Agent KB (Tang et al., arXiv 2507.06229, 2025); Cognitive Kernel-Pro (Fang et al., arXiv 2508.00414, 2025); Magentic-One (Fourney et al., arXiv 2411.04468, 2024); CAMEL (Li et al., NeurIPS 2023); OS-Copilot/FRIDAY (Wu et al., arXiv 2402.07456, 2024); HuggingFace smolagents (2025); communication-centric MAS survey (Yan et al., arXiv 2502.14321, 2025).

CODE: none (a GitHub repository is linked: https://github.com/Coral-Protocol/Anemoi). The consensus step is only given in notation: vi(R*) ∈ {approve, reject}, aggregated as C({vi}). No aggregation rule is stated.

FIGURES: Best single candidate is Figure 1 (p2), "Architecture of the Anemoi: a semi-centralized multi-agent system based on the A2A communication MCP server from Coral Protocol." It shows the thread-based all-to-all topology around the planner, which is faster to read than the prose. Fig 2 (p4) is a similar overview, and Fig 3 (p8) is a donut chart of win attributions. I did not view the images, only the captions.

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean, though the abstract text has fused words and the Table 3 bold markers merge into the numbers (e.g. "26.9250.30" means 26.92 and 50.30; "71.70 52.3315.3852.73" means 71.70, 52.33, 15.38, 52.73). Abstract and Table 3 disagree on OWL-rep (43.63 vs 43.64). No embedded instructions found. The percentages in Figs 3 and 4 were read from the text, not from the images.
